angle: Veteran pastor and pastoral counsellor. What a pastor feels when he opens a Bible app is that he is on duty again. Every surface asks him to produce something for someone else. The research says he is lonelier than he was (Barna: 65%, up from 42% in 2015) and that 38% thought about quitting in the past year, while 70% of him is already spending 8+ hours a week on Sunday. So the design question is not "what tools does he need" — the app already has more tools than he uses. It is "does this app know the difference between the pastor and the man". The app's own greeting already says the right sentence to him. Everything below it currently contradicts it.
thesis: Daily Word is where the pastor reads for himself, and the clean hand-off to where he works. Hold the first screenful for him — greeting, today's chapter already open, one question that is about him and not his church — then give him Sunday, below the reading, loaded and honest. Two changes carry most of the value and both are copy plus a gate, not a rebuild: the AI is framed and footered as a study assistant that finds and explains but never writes the message (the research calls this the highest-leverage copy change in the app), and the sources behind every commentary and lexicon result become visible on the reading screen instead of buried in Settings. Two things get removed because they fight the persona: the dead fabricated campus-count section that would put an invented number next to the real one, and a "Talk It Through" button that invites his heart into an AI whose own system prompt refuses feelings. Sermon prep stays off-app in Pastors Sermon Prep, per Ashley's 9 Sep ruling; Daily Word's job at the boundary is to hand over something already gathered.
principles: The first screenful belongs to the man, not the pastor. Greeting, reading, one question. Sunday appears after that, never before it.
Never print a number the app did not measure. One invented figure next to one real figure destroys both.
The assistant finds and explains. The pastor writes the message. Say so on the screen, not in Settings.
Every source names itself where it is read — name and licence, one line, under the text.
Do not rebuild sermon prep here. Gather well, hand over cleanly, get out of the way (Ashley, 9 Sep 2026).
Nothing in this path may shame him: no streak scold, no catch-up pile, no graduation prompt, no productivity guilt dressed as encouragement.
Comfort must reach him without him ever choosing it. He will not pick the comfort card on a good day, and on a bad day he will not go looking.

journey.day0: He taps the Leader card in the one path sheet — one tap saves as a real choice (source onboarding/settings) and opens Home immediately. No sign-in demanded to read. Home lands with today's chapter already expanded (credit-free arrival seed, bypasses handleRead) — if he has no plan and no reading slots, the rotating PASTOR_CHAPTERS floor means the hero is never empty. Below the reading: one question, then the Preach card, then a single quiet offer of a plan. He can finish a first session without making one decision.
journey.first_session: Three to six minutes. He reads. If a line lands he long-presses it and files it "To sermon" — the only capture gesture in the path, and it works from the hero, the plan passages and the commentary. Between You & God asks him one question. Today it may be about his church; two days in five it is about him. He writes two lines or he doesn't. He sees the Preach card say what is waiting for Sunday and does not tap it. That is a good first session.
journey.return_visit: Chapter re-seeds open on today's passage, same translation, commentary tab where he left it. Greeting carries the day count with no exclamation and no threat. Preach card now reads "2 filed since Sunday". Nothing new is announced; nothing asks to be set up again. The plan wizard has self-dismissed the moment any plan exists, from any device.
journey.week2: By day 7-10 he has filed four or five passages and opened the sources list at least once — the two behaviours that predict he stays. One prompt arrives, once: the app has watched when he actually opens and offers to move his reminder there. Thursday or Friday he taps Preach with a loaded bag rather than a blind jump. The soul-side questions have started landing; if one of them got a real answer written down, that is the retention event that matters more than the streak.
journey.missed_day: He buried someone on Thursday and did not open the app. Friday the single streak freeze bridges it silently (streak.ts, one freeze, replenished after 7 days). The greeting says Day 9, not "you lost your streak". No missed reading is queued, no catch-up card appears, nothing asks where he was. If he misses three days the count resets to 1 with no comment and no badge lost.
journey.seasonal: He is the one who runs the church-wide read, so the seasonal moment is the other side of it: he sets a preaching focus, publishes Sunday's notes through the staff intake, and his campus sees the plan and the notes without a developer touching anything. His own path stays exactly as it is during a season — no campaign banners land on his reading screen.

comfort_access: One line at the foot of Home, and the same line under any soul question in Between You & God: "Hard day? Open comfort." It opens the comfort reading as an overlay over his own path — one passage, slow audio first, low stimulus, no streak, no count, no "complete", toolbar Note and Close only. It must not call saveSetup, must not write dw_setup, must not stamp a real choice, and must not go through handleRead. He stays a pastor when he closes it. This matters more for him than for any other persona: 38% of pastors considered quitting in the past year, and a pastor will never choose the comfort card on a good day or go looking for it on a bad one. The "Feeling Stronger?" graduation prompt is removed for good and never returns, here or anywhere.
reminders: One a day, never two. For the first week it fires at the hour he set. After 7 recorded opens the app compares his actual open times to his set hour and, if they differ by more than an hour, asks once: "You mostly open around 6:20 am. Move your reminder there?" — accepted by tap only, never auto-applied, never asked again either way. Copy stays the existing neutral scripture-snippet templates; no pastor-specific push copy, and nothing that mentions a streak, a miss, or a day he owes. A missed day is bridged silently by the existing freeze; three missed days reset the count to 1 with no comment. If he turns notifications off, nothing in the app nags him about it. Note that push cannot be verified on a deploy preview — only localhost or prod (pushSupported allowlists futuresdailyword.com/www/localhost).

open_decisions: The Between You & God bank: approve the 8 soul questions as drafted (or rewrite them), and set the ratio — 8 soul to 15 work means roughly two days in five are about him. Content Claude drafts, Ashley approves, per the standing rule.

Whether the Preach card may ever show a modelled figure ("about 3 hours saved this week") or stays counted facts only. The research asks for minutes saved; the app's own history says never print a number it did not measure.

How the filed passages cross the origin boundary to Pastors Sermon Prep: clipboard only (works today, no integration), or Prep reads dw_sermon_prep from user_data when signed in with the same email. Needs his word on what Prep can read.
Does the pastor's Weekly Review land on Sunday as it does now, or on Monday? Sunday morning is the one morning he has no space, but nothing in the research settles it.
Who at each campus receives a prayer request, and whether a pastor sees the actual requests behind the prayer-requests tile or only the count. The research names this as his call.
Whether the Leader card's promise line may change on the path sheet — it is opening-screen-adjacent copy and the sheet's height budget is fixed at ~481px (537 with the sign-out row).
risks: Moving the Preach card is a Home IA reshape and falls under the preview gate: it ships behind a deploy preview link Ashley approves before merge, never straight to main. It also touches all five paths, so the Sunday-window gate that keeps the card above the reading for I'm New QR guests must land in the same PR or Sunday visitors lose their route to notes.

home-pastor-floor.test.ts:63-70 pins the exact preach_card_sub string and the PREP_URL assign. Changing the sub copy breaks that test — update the assertion deliberately to the new string; do not loosen it to a substring match, because it is what stops the deep-link from silently reverting to the congregation chooser.

Moving the question bank to /books/ without bumping CACHE_NAME, STATIC_CACHE and SW_VERSION together means returning pastors keep the old questions forever. This is the documented trap that already bit /books once.

The AI answer footer must stay one warm line. The research on the adjacent persona found 81% of mental-health apps carry liability disclaimers instead of real help — a legal wall under every answer would do more damage to trust than no footer at all.

A soul question can land on a pastor in a hard week. Every one must read as a friend asking, not a diagnostic. If any of the eight cannot be read aloud to a pastor who is thinking about quitting, it does not ship.

Removing campus_count is safe today because the section is unmounted, but the same key still sits in another persona's sectionOrder at persona-config.ts:341. Leaving the component in the tree means a future sectionOrder wiring lights up a fabricated number on a screen that was deliberately cleaned of one.

The behaviour-inferred hour needs open times stored somewhere. Store the last N open hours locally and derive the median on device — do not build a new synced record for it, and never rebuild a dw_* record from React state at mount.

The sources sheet and the comfort overlay both open over a full-screen host. Use useSubView alone, mounted with a live open prop — useSubView plus useModalA11y/aria-modal nests focus traps and breaks Android back, and conditional mounting orphans a history entry per close.
